full_judgment: 6. Mr. Harendra Nath Nondy, the learned advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that the suit is barred by limitation as P.W.1 i.e. the plaintiff himself admitted that he tried to record his name in the S.A. record according to him in Jessore area S.A. survey started in 1956 and published in 1957 and knowledge of wrong recording must be during that time; thus institution of the suit in 1980, nearly after 23 years of plaintiffs knowledge of wrong recording is hopelessly barred by limitation. Secondly, he submits that P.W. 1st admission that other than 3 Katas of his paternal property he did not purchase or acquire any property supports the suggestion of the defendants that the plaintiff had no right, title and interest in the suit land and hence he did not record his name. Thirdly, he submits that recording of Godai's name being existing for long 30 years, and supported by the dakhilas, the presumption should have been that the defendants have title and possession in the suit land. According to him the rent receipts filed by the defendants are corollary evidences of title and possession and thus the rent receipts of the defendants following the title of Godai Molla being not considered by the courts below the findings and decision arrived at are erroneous and as such liable to be set aside. Relying on the case of Erfam Ali Bs. Joynal Abedin Mia and others reported in 35 DLR (AD) 216 he submits that when on finding of fact not based on evidence or is based on utterly inadequate evidence or inconsistent with the evidence on record, the High Court is justified in interfering with the same when such misreading of evidence is apparent. According to him the finding of the court of appeal below being based on inadequate evidence the same has resulted error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Mr. Nondy then submits that the Court of Appeal below misread and misconstrued the evidences of P.Ws. (who were produced as witnesses, without issuing summons) and came to an erroneous decision without considering that out of the five witnesses, three of them stated that they do not know the suit and. Thus he submits that the finding and decision based on such evidences which are not legally admissible are liable to be set aside. He submits that Rashik Lal Ghoseson of Kunja Behari Ghose, was produced as P.W. 4, who admitted that his father Kunju Bihari Ghose surrendered possession of the suit land to the superior Land Lord and as such the court of appeal below without considering this aspect of the evidence, came to an erroneous finding that the plaintiff has been able to prove his case, which is erroneous. The next contention of Mr. Nondy is that the courts below did not consider Exhibit 'C', the judgment passed in Second Appeal No. 572 of 1997. Lastly he submits that the learned Judge failed to consider that without asking for consequential relief simple declaration of this nature is not maintainable. Thus according to him the judgment and decree complained of is erroneous and has resulted error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and as such the same are liable to be set aside.
